# DRM ground-truth fixtures

These fixtures let the Rust/WASM DRM decoder be verified without a live shortwave
DRM broadcast (which is not reliably receivable on a SAN-90 in a lab).

## `drm_modeB_so3_48k.f32` + `manifest.json`

A synthesised DRM30 signal with **known** content: robustness mode B, spectrum
occupancy 3 (10 kHz), 64-QAM SM MSC, 16-QAM SDC, long interleaving, EEP protection
level 1. The SDC carries a station label `SAN90 DRM TEST` and an AAC (24 kHz SBR
mono) audio service; the FAC carries service id `0x123456`, one audio service, no
data services. Full ground truth lives in `manifest.json`.

- `drm_modeB_so3_48k.f32` — interleaved I/Q `float32` (little-endian), 48 kHz
  complex, 6.0 s (288000 complex samples).
- `manifest.json` — format, signal/FAC/SDC/MSC ground truth, and the generator's
  self-check result.

## Provenance and licence

The fixture is **data** emitted by running the DecDRM transmitter:

- Project: https://github.com/CasualArclamp/DecDRM (v0.5.1, commit
  `b1fbd87f3d3e4709ff838d5120724fb4506253f6`), licence **GPL-2.0-or-later**.
- Generator: `crates/decdrm-core/examples/gen_fixture.rs` (written for this repo;
  transmits the signal, then decodes it back with the DecDRM receiver as a
  self-check).

The I/Q samples describe a signal defined by the ETSI ES 201 980 standard and are
not GPL source; only the *generator tool* is GPL. DecDRM is therefore kept out of
this repository and used solely as an external fixture generator / oracle — the
in-tree Rust/WASM decoder is an independent implementation.

## `aac_sine_24k.{drm,ga,json}` — DRM AAC audio fixture

A run of 9 re-serialised DRM AAC access units plus their original MPEG-4 GA
access units, used to verify the **audio** stage of the DRM receive chain
(MSC → AAC access units → PCM) independently of the OFDM/FAC/SDC stages.

- `aac_sine_24k.drm` — 9 DRM AAC access units (36 bytes each), concatenated:
  the GA frames re-serialised to DRM syntax (VCB11 section data, HCR spectral
  data, `aac_crc_bits`).
- `aac_sine_24k.ga` — the original 9 GA AAC-LC access units (320 bytes each),
  the lossless reference.
- `aac_sine_24k.json` — frame sizes, codec config, and the verification result.

The signal is a 1 kHz sine, AAC-LC 24 kHz mono, 64 kbit/s CBR, 960-sample
frames (the DRM transform length). Generated by `tools/gen_drm_aac_fixture.py`
from FDK-AAC (960-sample encoder patch) GA frames re-serialised by
`tools/drm_aac_reserialize.py`. Verify with `tools/verify_drm_aac.c`:

```sh
cc -O2 -I <fdk>/libAACdec/include -I <fdk>/libSYS/include \
   -I <fdk>/libMpegTPDec/include -I <fdk>/libFDK/include \
   -I <fdk>/libSBRdec/include -I <fdk>/libSACdec/include \
   -I <fdk>/libPCMutils/include -I <fdk>/libArithCoding/include \
   -I <fdk>/libDRCdec/include \
   tools/verify_drm_aac.c <fdk>/build/libfdk-aac.a -lm -o verify_drm_aac
./verify_drm_aac tests/fixtures/drm/aac_sine_24k.drm \
                  tests/fixtures/drm/aac_sine_24k.ga 36 320
# 9 frames: mismatch=0 energy=139955180 -> OK
```

The DRM decode matches the GA decode bit-for-bit (`mismatch=0`) and is
non-silent — the re-serialiser is lossless. (The decoder has a two-frame
priming delay, so the first two decoded frames are silent; the assertion
totals energy across all 9.)

## `drm_modeB_so3_48k_aac.f32` — end-to-end audio fixture

Identical to the main fixture (Mode B / SO3, 10 kHz, 64-QAM SM MSC, 16-QAM SDC,
long interleaving), except the MSC payload is a **real 24 kHz AAC audio super
frame** (10 re-serialised DRM AAC access units of a 1 kHz sine) instead of the
xorshift bit stream. This exercises the full receive chain through to PCM:
`DrmReceiver → deframe_audio → decode_audio → audio_pcm`, asserted non-silent by
`wasm/tests/drm_fixture.rs::fixture_deframes_real_aac_audio` (native deframe) and
`frontend/src/__tests__/drmAudioEndToEnd.test.ts` (wasm32 AAC decode through the
`websa_dsp_drm_audio_pcm` ABI).

Generated by the DecDRM `gen_fixture.rs` example with its MSC payload replaced by
`tools/gen_drm_aac_fixture.py` + the DRM AAC re-serialiser; see the example's
comments and `tools/drm_aac_reserialize.py`.

## Regenerating

Clone DecDRM (outside this repo), drop in the `gen_fixture.rs` example, and run:

```sh
cargo build --release -p decdrm-core --example gen_fixture
./target/release/examples/gen_fixture B 3 6.0 tests/fixtures/drm/drm_modeB_so3_48k.f32
```

Then paste the printed summary back into `manifest.json`'s `self_check` block if it
changed. The parameters are `gen_fixture <mode A-D> <so 0-5> <seconds> <out.f32>`.

## Real off-air recordings

For later validation against real broadcasts, the DecDRM test suite references a set
of off-air DRM recordings (e.g. `DW_ModeB_10kHz.flac`, `RTL_ModeB_10kHz.flac`,
`Deutschlandradio_ModeA_10kHz.flac`) with known mode/occupancy; see
`crates/decdrm-core/tests/recordings.rs` in DecDRM. Those recordings are not
committed there and are intentionally out of scope for the committed fixture set.
